links.targetTitle: Uniswap V3 price bounds are anchored to the pool's TWAP tick

title: Maximum tick deviation is the only governance-configured control on Uniswap v3 swap execution quality
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.3.3 ends with an unusually candid sentence: "The maximum tick deviation is the only governance-configured control on the swap's execution quality; the minimum amount received has no equivalent governance floor beyond being non-zero."

The swap therefore carries two guards of very different strength. The tick deviation must "fall within the configured maximum for the pool," so governance sets a hard ceiling on how far execution may drift from the TWAP. The minimum amount received is supplied per call by the Allocator and is only required to be non-zero — a bound the caller sets on itself.

The practical implication is that within the tick band, a relayer can accept an arbitrarily poor fill. Defence against a *malicious* operator on this path rests entirely on the tick configuration and the rate limit that caps how much can be sold; the min-out parameter defends only against passive market movement between submission and execution.

That the Atlas states this rather than presenting both parameters as equivalent safeguards is what makes it useful. It tells a reviewer where to concentrate: the per-pool tick configuration is load-bearing, and calibrating it loosely removes the only governance-side guarantee on swap pricing.
description: The Atlas notes the minimum amount received has no governance floor beyond being non-zero, leaving the caller free to accept any fill the TWAP bound permits.
